questions.stem_html:
A 50-year-old man has years of migratory arthralgias followed by weight loss, diarrhea, and abdominal distention. Small-bowel biopsy shows villi expanded by foamy macrophages containing periodic acid-Schiff-positive, acid-fast-negative material. Electron microscopy reveals bacillary structures within macrophages.

Which organism is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation_html: Tropheryma whipplei accumulates within lamina-propria macrophages, distorts villi, and impairs nutrient absorption. PAS positivity with acid-fast negativity and preceding migratory arthralgia are classic. The combined arthralgia-malabsorption sequence and PAS-positive foamy macrophages identify Whipple disease.

wrong_choice_explanations.1: MAC can fill macrophages in advanced HIV but is acid-fast positive and occurs in profound immunodeficiency.
wrong_choice_explanations.2: Giardia adheres to the mucosal surface and causes malabsorption without PAS-positive bacilli-laden macrophages.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: Histoplasma can reside in macrophages but is a budding yeast and is not the classic cause of arthralgia followed by Whipple enteropathy.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: Cryptosporidium organisms line the apical epithelial surface and are identified with modified acid-fast staining.

questions.educational_objective: Recognize Whipple disease from migratory arthralgia, malabsorption, and PAS-positive acid-fast-negative macrophages containing Tropheryma whipplei.
